{{short description|Concept in Hopf algebra and weak Hopf algebra}}

In [[quantum group]], [[Hopf algebra]] and [[weak Hopf algebra]], the '''Doi-Hopf module''' is a crucial construction that has many applications. It's named after Japanese mathematician [[Yukio Doi]] ([[土井 幸雄]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=土井 幸雄 (Yukio Doi) - マイポータル - researchmap |url=https://researchmap.jp/read0010096 |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=researchmap.jp}}</ref>) and  German  mathematician [[Heinz Hopf]]. The concept was introduce by Doi in his 1992 paper "unifying Hopf modules<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Doi |first=Yukio |date=1992-12-15 |title=Unifying Hopf modules |journal=Journal of Algebra |language=en |volume=153 |issue=2 |pages=373–385 |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(92)90160-N |issn=0021-8693|doi-access=free }}</ref>".

== Doi-Hopf module ==

A right Doi-Hopf datum is a triple <math>(H,A,C)</math> with <math>H</math> a Hopf algebra, <math>A</math> a left <math>H</math>-comodule algebra, and <math>C</math> a right <math>H</math>-module coalgebra. A left-right  Doi-Hopf <math>(H,A,C)</math>-module <math>M</math> is a left <math>A</math>-module and a right <math>C</math>-comodule via <math>\beta: M\to M\otimes C</math> such that <math>\beta(am)=\sum a_{(0)}m_{[0]}\otimes a_{(1)}\rightharpoonup m_{[1]}</math> for all <math>a\in A,m\in M</math>. The subscript is the Sweedler notation.

A left Doi-Hopf datum is a triple <math>(H,A,C)</math> with <math>H</math> a Hopf algebra, <math>A</math> a right <math>H</math>-comodule algebra, and <math>C</math> a left <math>H</math>-module coalgebra. A Doi-Hopf module can be defined similarly.

== Doi-Hopf module in weak Hopf algebra ==

The generalization of Doi-Hopf module in weak Hopf algebra case is given by Gabriella Böhm in 2000.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Böhm |first=Gabriella |date=2000-01-01 |title=Doi-hopf modules over weak hopf algebras |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00927870008827113 |journal=Communications in Algebra |volume=28 |issue=10 |pages=4687–4698 |doi=10.1080/00927870008827113 |arxiv=math/9905027 |s2cid=123012465 |issn=0092-7872}}</ref>
